% The three faces, loaded from the files vendored in this extension.
%
% Here rather than in _extension.yml's mainfont/sansfont/monofont keys,
% because pandoc LaTeX-ESCAPES the values of the matching *fontoptions keys:
% `Path=_extensions/...` reaches the .tex as `Path=\_extensions/...` and
% xelatex fails with "Missing \begin{document}" from inside \setsansfont.
% A header include is raw LaTeX and is passed through untouched.
%
% Loading by FILE, not by installed name: Atkinson Hyperlegible is not on any
% machine by default, so naming it would silently fall back to a generic sans
% -- and KOMA's scrartcl sets every heading through \sffamily, which makes
% the sans face the HEADING face. The static cuts are used rather than the
% variable AtkinsonHyperlegibleNext[wght].ttf because XeTeX reaches only a
% variable font's default instance, so bold and italic would be synthesised.
%
% Paths are relative to the .tex, which Quarto writes at the project root.
\usepackage{fontspec}
\setmainfont{Lora}[
  Path=_extensions/mariner/fonts/,
  Extension=.ttf,
  UprightFont=*-Regular, BoldFont=*-Bold,
  ItalicFont=*-Italic, BoldItalicFont=*-BoldItalic]
\setsansfont{AtkinsonHyperlegible}[
  Path=_extensions/mariner/fonts/,
  Extension=.ttf,
  UprightFont=*-Regular, BoldFont=*-Bold,
  ItalicFont=*-Italic, BoldItalicFont=*-BoldItalic]
\setmonofont{JetBrainsMono}[
  Path=_extensions/mariner/fonts/,
  Extension=.ttf,
  Scale=MatchLowercase,
  UprightFont=*-Regular, BoldFont=*-Bold,
  ItalicFont=*-Italic, BoldItalicFont=*-BoldItalic]

% Body copy in the theme's near-black rather than pure black.
\AtBeginDocument{\color{qmdink}}

% Headings in the primary colour. Quarto's default PDF class is KOMA's
% scrartcl, where `disposition` is the font element every heading level
% inherits from -- one line covers title, sections and subsections. The
% guard means a document that overrides documentclass still compiles, just
% without coloured headings.
\makeatletter
\@ifundefined{addtokomafont}{}{%
  \addtokomafont{disposition}{\color{qmdprimary}}%
  \addtokomafont{caption}{\small}%
  \addtokomafont{captionlabel}{\bfseries\color{qmdprimary}}%
}
\makeatother

% Deferred to \AtBeginDocument because a header include lands in the
% preamble BEFORE Quarto's template loads hyperref -- calling \hypersetup
% here directly fails with "Undefined control sequence".
\AtBeginDocument{%
  \hypersetup{colorlinks=true, linkcolor=qmdprimary,
    filecolor=qmdlink, urlcolor=qmdlink, citecolor=qmdlink}%
}

% Rules in booktabs tables in the primary colour rather than black. The test
% is \ifcsname rather than \@ifundefined on purpose: the body of
% \AtBeginDocument is tokenised where it is written, and "@" is not a letter
% in the preamble, so a \@... command inside it would be misparsed long
% before \makeatletter could take effect.
\AtBeginDocument{%
  \ifcsname arrayrulecolor\endcsname\arrayrulecolor{qmdprimary}\fi
}

% Document markup: the targets of the class names a document writes.
%
% Nothing reaches these commands on its own. Pandoc's LaTeX writer ignores
% span and div classes it does not recognise -- `[x]{.defn}` comes out as
% `{x}` and `::: {.def}` comes out as its own contents -- so the mapping from
% class to command is done by mariner-markup.lua, which the extension
% contributes as a filter. Renaming a command here means renaming it there.
%
% The command is \marineremph rather than \emph on purpose. Pandoc emits
% \emph{...} for ordinary markdown *italics*, so redefining \emph restyles
% every italic in the document -- underlined and bold -- rather than only the
% spans that asked for it.
\providecommand{\texorpdfstring}[2]{#1}
\DeclareRobustCommand{\defn}[1]{\textcolor{qmdprimary}{\underline{\textit{#1}}}}
\DeclareRobustCommand{\term}[1]{\textcolor{qmdprimary}{\textbf{#1}}}
\DeclareRobustCommand{\termref}[1]{\textcolor{qmdprimary}{\textit{#1}}}
\DeclareRobustCommand{\marineremph}[1]{\underline{\textbf{\textit{#1}}}}
% Font-switching spans, for setting a specimen of one family inside a
% document typeset in another. \setmainfont is the body face and
% \setsansfont the heading face, so these are the two that need naming.
\DeclareRobustCommand{\fontheadings}[1]{{\sffamily #1}}
\DeclareRobustCommand{\fontbody}[1]{{\rmfamily #1}}
\DeclareRobustCommand{\linkeddefn}[2]{%
  \texorpdfstring{\hypertarget{ref-#1}{\hyperlink{def-#1}{\defn{#2}}}}{\defn{#2}}}
\DeclareRobustCommand{\defanchor}[1]{\texorpdfstring{\hypertarget{def-#1}{}}{}}
\DeclareRobustCommand{\backlink}[1]{%
  \texorpdfstring{\hyperlink{ref-#1}{\textcolor{qmdprimary}{\small$\hookleftarrow$}}}{}}

% Definition and theorem blocks, entered from `::: {.def}` and `::: {.thm}`
% by the same filter.
%
% Built from \leftskip and \rule rather than a framing package: a tcolorbox
% or mdframed block cannot break across a page, and a definition that runs
% past the bottom of one would be pushed whole onto the next, leaving the
% page short. These break normally.
%
% \addvspace rather than \vspace so two adjacent blocks share one gap instead
% of stacking two.
\newenvironment{marinerdef}{%
  \par\addvspace{0.7\baselineskip}%
  \noindent{\color{qmdprimary}\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\nobreak
  \vspace{0.35\baselineskip}%
  \begingroup\leftskip=1.2em\relax\rightskip=1.2em\relax
}{%
  \par\endgroup\addvspace{0.7\baselineskip}%
}
\newenvironment{marinerthm}{%
  \par\addvspace{0.7\baselineskip}%
  \noindent{\color{qmdprimary}\rule{\linewidth}{0.8pt}}\par\nobreak
  \vspace{0.35\baselineskip}%
  \begingroup\leftskip=1.2em\relax\rightskip=1.2em\relax
}{%
  \par\endgroup\vspace{0.35\baselineskip}%
  \noindent{\color{qmdprimary}\rule{\linewidth}{0.8pt}}%
  \par\addvspace{0.7\baselineskip}%
}

% Floats stay in the section that introduces them.
%
% fig-pos is 'htbp' (set in _extension.yml) so that an oversized figure can
% move instead of running off the page -- but plain 'htbp' lets it move too
% far: LaTeX defers a figure it cannot fit, and the deferred ones then pile
% up on a later page AFTER the heading of the section that follows. Two
% figures and the next subsection title end up in the wrong order.
%
% \FloatBarrier flushes pending floats before each heading, which bounds the
% drift to the section that owns them. The float fractions are relaxed at the
% same time so a tall figure is accepted on a page with text rather than
% being deferred in the first place -- barriers alone would just turn the
% deferral into a half-empty page.
\usepackage{placeins}
\makeatletter
\AtBeginDocument{%
  \@ifundefined{section}{}{%
    \let\qmdorigsection\section
    \renewcommand{\section}{\FloatBarrier\qmdorigsection}}%
  \@ifundefined{subsection}{}{%
    \let\qmdorigsubsection\subsection
    \renewcommand{\subsection}{\FloatBarrier\qmdorigsubsection}}%
}
\makeatother
\renewcommand{\topfraction}{0.9}
\renewcommand{\bottomfraction}{0.8}
\renewcommand{\textfraction}{0.07}
\renewcommand{\floatpagefraction}{0.75}

% The title block and the contents own the first page; the body starts on a
% fresh one. Attached to \tableofcontents rather than written as a \clearpage
% in the document, so it happens only when there IS a table of contents -- a
% document with toc: false gets no stray blank page.
%
% Deferred to \AtBeginDocument for the same reason \hypersetup above is:
% both KOMA and hyperref patch \tableofcontents themselves at the start of
% the document, so a plain \renewcommand in the preamble is silently thrown
% away and the break never happens.
\AtBeginDocument{%
  \let\qmdorigtableofcontents\tableofcontents
  \renewcommand{\tableofcontents}{\qmdorigtableofcontents\clearpage}%
}

% The brand mark, in the bottom-right corner of the first page.
%
% eso-pic's starred form applies to the CURRENT page only, so this marks the
% title page and leaves the body clean -- a logo repeated on every page of a
% long report is noise. The origin is the bottom-left of the paper and \put
% positions the bottom-left of the BOX, so the vertical coordinate is just the
% clearance from the paper edge; \LenToUnit converts a LaTeX length into the
% bare number \put wants.
%
% Bottom rather than top because it cannot then collide with the title block,
% which a top-right mark does on any document whose title runs long enough to
% reach the margin.
%
% The width below is DERIVED: 0.25in tall, times the image's own aspect
% ratio. Nothing here has to know which mark is in the medium slot.
%
% The path is relative to the .tex, which Quarto writes at the project root,
% so it reaches the copy vendored inside the extension and needs nothing
% copied into the project. \includegraphics cannot read SVG, which is why the
% bundled marks are PNG.
\usepackage{eso-pic}
\usepackage{graphicx}
\newlength{\qmdlogowidth}
\setlength{\qmdlogowidth}{1.4038in}
\IfFileExists{_extensions/mariner/logos/BU_BrandMark_Horz_Green.png}{%
  \AddToShipoutPictureFG*{%
    \put(\LenToUnit{\dimexpr\paperwidth-1in-\qmdlogowidth\relax},%
         \LenToUnit{0.4in}){%
      \includegraphics[width=\qmdlogowidth]{_extensions/mariner/logos/BU_BrandMark_Horz_Green.png}}%
  }%
}{}
